title: Idempotency Keys, Circuit Breakers & Backoff Jitter
subtitle: Preventing duplicate charges and cascading retry storms
overview: Networks are unreliable: mobile users tap Pay twice or experience a timeout *after* the server processed the charge, while blind client retries multiply an upstream blip into a 10x retry storm that prevents recovery. Idempotency keys make retries safe, while Circuit Breakers + Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter protect failing dependencies.
firstPrinciplesStory: A third-party Fraud API degrades from 40ms to 5s latency. Your Checkout service times out at 2s and immediately retries 3 times—tripling traffic onto the struggling Fraud API! Meanwhile, every Checkout pod ties up all worker threads waiting on 2s timeouts, cascading the outage across your entire site, and anxious customers hit 'Pay' again getting double-charged! Bounded timeouts, Circuit Breakers, Jittered Backoff, and Idempotency Keys turn partial failures into graceful containment.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: An **Idempotency Key** is writing a unique receipt number (`req_991`) on a check: even if the bank teller accidentally processes a photocopy twice, they see `#991` already cleared and hand back the exact original receipt without taking another dollar. A **Circuit Breaker** is your home electrical breaker tripping open during a short circuit so the whole house doesn't catch fire—letting a few trial requests through (`Half-Open`, 3 in this lesson) 15 seconds later before restoring power.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Client sends `Idempotency-Key: uuid` on `POST /charges`. Server atomically claims `(user_id, key)` inside the transaction (or Redis lock) and stores the serialized response; duplicate keys replay the cached response, return `409 Conflict` while the first request is still in flight, and return `422` if the same key arrives with a different payload (the IETF Idempotency-Key draft's codes). Outbound clients wrap downstream RPCs with a `CircuitBreaker(Closed -> Open -> Half-Open)` + `sleep = random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))` full jitter.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Never use bare `base * 2^attempt` without random jitter—if 10,000 clients drop together, deterministic backoff makes all 10,000 hammer the server in synchronized waves at 1s, 2s, 4s! Also enforce **Retry Budgets** (cap retries at ~10–20% of normal traffic) so nested microservice retries (`3^3 = 27x` amplification!) never amplify outages.

ddiaAnchors.chapter: DDIA Ch. 8 & 12 · Partial Failures & End-to-End Correctness
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Because TCP/HTTP timeouts cannot distinguish 'never arrived' from 'succeeded but ack lost', end-to-end idempotency is mandatory.

pragmaticTips.tip: An RPC call without a deadline/timeout is a memory and thread-pool leak waiting for the first slow dependency.
pragmaticTips.application: Set tight per-hop timeouts + circuit breakers + bulkhead thread pools isolating slow external APIs.

keyTakeaways: Idempotency keys let callers safely retry ambiguous timeouts without duplicate side effects.
Full jitter spreads synchronized retry waves evenly across time, preventing thundering-herd retry storms.
Circuit breakers fail fast (`Open`) when error rate crosses threshold and probe safely (`Half-Open`) before restoring traffic.

nodes.label: Mobile Client
nodes.summary: Sends persistent UUID Idempotency-Key across automatic network retries.
failureModes: Generating a fresh UUID inside the retry loop breaks idempotency completely!

nodes.label: Checkout + Circuit Breaker
nodes.summary: Checks Idempotency store atomically and guards external Fraud/Bank RPCs via Circuit Breaker.
failureModes: Retrying on HTTP 400 validation errors or without jitter wastes resources

nodes.label: Idempotency & Ledger DB
nodes.summary: Atomically inserts idempotency key alongside ledger debit and saves JSON response for replays.
failureModes: Using a volatile non-persistent Redis cache risks losing keys right before crash

nodes.label: External Fraud / PSP API
nodes.summary: Third-party external API susceptible to latency spikes and 5xx brownouts.
whenToUse: External risk checks or payment processors
failureModes: Slow 10s hangs exhaust caller connection pools without timeouts & circuit breaking

steps.payloadInspector: POST /v1/charges | Idempotency-Key: k_991 | SHA256(body)=0x91ab -> INSERT idempotency_keys(k_991, status=IN_PROGRESS)
steps.inspectorNote: The key is claimed atomically with status IN_PROGRESS, and the body hash is stored with it, so reusing `k_991` with a different amount is rejected with 422 Unprocessable Entity.

steps.info: Circuit Breaker CLOSED -> Fraud check passes in 35ms (deadline=800ms)
steps.inspectorNote: Strict 800ms timeout prevents slow upstream connections from leaking threads.

steps.info: Duplicate POST with k_991 arrives while the first is still running -> 409 Conflict, retry later
steps.payloadInspector: SELECT status FROM idempotency_keys WHERE key='k_991' -> IN_PROGRESS -> HTTP 409 (Retry-After: 1)
steps.inspectorNote: The hardest case: there is no saved response yet to replay. Without the IN_PROGRESS claim, both requests would call the payment provider.

steps.info: Tx commits charge AND saves 200 OK JSON against k_991 -> network drops response!
steps.payloadInspector: DB COMMIT OK: {charge_id: 'ch_77', status: 'PAID'} saved in idempotency_keys
steps.inspectorNote: Suppose Wi-Fi drops right before the client gets the 200 OK—so the client retries with `k_991`!

predictPrompt.prompt: Client retries `POST /v1/charges` with the SAME `Idempotency-Key: k_991` 2 seconds later. What does Checkout Service do?
predictPrompt.hint: Check whether it needs to call the external Fraud/Payment API a second time.
predictPrompt.reveal: It finds `k_991` already committed in `idemp-db`, skips charging or calling Fraud API again, and replays the exact saved `{charge_id: 'ch_77', status: 'PAID'}` response!

chaosScenarios.title: External Fraud API Slowdown -> Breaker Trips OPEN + Full Jitter Probe
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Fraud API latency spikes to 5,000ms, causing >50% 800ms timeouts across a 10-second sliding window.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Circuit Breaker trips OPEN, immediately shedding calls in <1ms via fallback heuristic for 15s, then lets 3 trial requests through in HALF-OPEN before closing.

steps.info: Error rate 62% (>50% threshold) -> Circuit Breaker switches CLOSED -> OPEN
steps.payloadInspector: Breaker State: OPEN (15s cooldown) -> Fast-fail / fallback rule active (<1ms)
steps.inspectorNote: Failing fast frees Checkout worker threads immediately AND gives the struggling Fraud API breathing room to recover.

steps.info: After 15s, Breaker lets 3 trial requests through (HALF-OPEN) -> all 200 OK -> CLOSED
steps.payloadInspector: 3/3 trial requests succeeded in 32ms -> Breaker State: CLOSED
steps.inspectorNote: Controlled canary probing verifies real recovery without unleashing full traffic immediately.

tradeoffs.option: DB-Backed Idempotency + Circuit Breaker + Full Jitter
pros: Prevents cascading thread-pool exhaustion & retry storms
cons: Needs periodic TTL cleanup of old idempotency rows
tradeoffs.bestFor: All payment, order, booking, and third-party API integrations

cons: Multiplies outages exponentially across microservice hops (thundering retry storm)
